Justification: Required to govern the ISMS and set mandatory direction for all staff and contractors.
Implementation evidence: Information security policy v1.0 approved by the CEO on 15 December 2026; 13 topic-specific policies approved by February 2027.

Justification: Accountability must be assigned for the ISMS, risks, assets, and controls.
Implementation evidence: Roles and RACI approved 15 December 2026; role holders confirmed and deputies named.

Justification: Production changes and privileged actions require independent review to prevent unilateral control.
Implementation evidence: Branch protection with required review; emergency changes require CTO approval and post-implementation review; production access separated from support duties.

Justification: Managers must enforce policy and hold staff accountable.
Implementation evidence: Policy acknowledgement by all staff; management review minutes record decisions and actions; disciplinary process in the employee handbook.

Justification: PDPL, cyber crime law, and health regulation require contact with regulators and law enforcement.
Implementation evidence: Authority contact list in the incident response plan; legal counsel acts as the formal channel.

Justification: Sector and vendor advisories inform threat awareness and vulnerability response.
Implementation evidence: Subscriptions to vendor security bulletins and Egyptian cybersecurity advisories; owner recorded in the ISMS roles.

Justification: Healthcare threat intelligence is relevant to phishing, ransomware, and exploitation risk.
Implementation evidence: GuardDuty findings, vendor advisories, and sector bulletins are reviewed weekly; no dedicated threat intelligence platform or formal collection plan.

Justification: New features, projects, and suppliers can introduce risk that must be assessed before delivery.
Implementation evidence: Security review gate in the product lifecycle; DPIA trigger for personal-data changes; change records sampled.

Annex A control: Inventory of information and other associated assets
Justification: A complete asset inventory is required to scope controls and risk assessments.
Implementation evidence: Asset register NH-REG-001 with 50 assets, owners, criticality, and data sensitivity; reviewed quarterly.

Annex A control: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
Justification: Staff and contractors use company and personal devices to access patient data.
Implementation evidence: Acceptable use and information handling policy; 100 percent acknowledgement recorded.

Justification: Devices, fobs, and credentials must be returned when employment or engagement ends.
Implementation evidence: Offboarding checklist completed for 6 leavers sampled in Q1 2027; asset return register maintained.

Justification: Patient, personal, financial, and business information require different handling.
Implementation evidence: Four-level classification scheme (Public, Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential) in the information handling policy; data inventory classified.

Justification: Labels make handling rules visible and support DLP and access decisions.
Implementation evidence: Labels applied to documents, repositories, and ticket templates; several legacy documents and SaaS records remain unlabelled.

Justification: Patient and customer data is transferred by email, API, and file sharing.
Implementation evidence: TLS 1.2 or higher in transit; DLP rules for email and chat; transfer rules in the information handling policy.

Justification: Access to patient data and production systems must follow least privilege.
Implementation evidence: Role-based access model; access control policy; role matrix for Admin Panel and AWS.

Justification: Unique identities are required for accountability and access review.
Implementation evidence: Google Workspace for staff identity; IAM Identity Center for AWS; unique accounts for all staff and contractors.

Justification: Credentials and keys are the primary path to patient data and production systems.
Implementation evidence: Company password manager; MFA enforced; secrets in Secrets Manager; shared credentials removed and keys rotated.

Justification: Joiner, mover, and leaver access must be provisioned, reviewed, and removed.
Implementation evidence: Offboarding procedure and quarterly access reviews operate; one Freshdesk leaver account remained active at internal audit (NC-02).

Justification: Critical services depend on suppliers with access to Nabd data.
Implementation evidence: Supplier register, tiering, assessments, and contracts with security requirements.

Annex A control: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
Justification: Contracts must allocate security, privacy, and audit obligations.
Implementation evidence: New template includes security, DPA, breach notification, and audit rights; legacy agreements are being amended in 2027.

Annex A control: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
Justification: Code dependencies and CI/CD services form part of the delivery chain.
Implementation evidence: Dependency and container scanning, branch protection, and signed images; supplier chain mapping is not yet complete for all third-party services.

Annex A control: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
Justification: Supplier performance and security posture can change during the contract.
Implementation evidence: Annual review schedule and SLA monitoring in place; 5 of 7 tier 1 assessments complete at 15 April 2027.

Annex A control: Information security for use of cloud services
Justification: The platform is entirely cloud-hosted and relies on shared responsibility.
Implementation evidence: AWS and Google assurance reports collected; cloud configuration standards; supplier register entries for AWS, Google, and GitHub.

Annex A control: Information security incident management planning and preparation
Justification: Incidents affecting patient data or availability must be handled consistently.
Implementation evidence: Incident management policy and incident response plan approved; severity matrix, on-call rota, and templates in place.

Annex A control: Assessment and decision on information security events
Justification: Events must be triaged consistently to determine severity and response.
Implementation evidence: Triage checklist and severity matrix; incident register maintained by the ISMS Manager.

Justification: Response actions must be defined to contain, eradicate, and recover.
Implementation evidence: Runbooks for account compromise, ransomware, data exposure, and availability incidents; two exercises completed.

Justification: Post-incident review is required to prevent recurrence.
Implementation evidence: Post-incident review template; lessons recorded in the incident register and reviewed by the Security and Risk Committee.

Justification: Evidence may be needed for legal, regulatory, and disciplinary purposes.
Implementation evidence: Evidence handling section in the incident response plan; chain-of-custody form; legal counsel involvement defined.

Justification: Security controls must remain effective during outages and recovery.
Implementation evidence: Business continuity and disaster recovery plan includes security requirements for degraded operations.

Justification: Contracted availability and recovery expectations require tested readiness.
Implementation evidence: RPO 1 hour and RTO 8 hours approved; restore test completed 14 March 2027; tabletop exercise completed.

Annex A control: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
Justification: PDPL, cyber crime law, health rules, CBE requirements, and customer contracts apply.
Implementation evidence: Legal and contractual requirements register maintained by the CFO with counsel; reviewed annually and on change.

Justification: Nabd uses third-party software, open-source dependencies, and contractor code.
Implementation evidence: Open-source licence review in dependency management; contractor IP assignment in agreements; software licence inventory.

Justification: Patient, employee, contractual, and security records must be protected and retained.
Implementation evidence: Retention schedule, access controls, encrypted backups, and records storage rules.

Justification: Nabd is a controller and processor of sensitive health and personal data.
Implementation evidence: Privacy policy, DPAs, records of processing, DSR procedure, and DPO appointed; DPIA and cross-border transfer assessment are in legal review.

Justification: An independent view is required before certification and annually thereafter.
Implementation evidence: Internal audit performed 12 to 16 April 2027 by an independent contracted auditor; report issued 23 April 2027.

Annex A control: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
Justification: Compliance must be monitored, not assumed.
Implementation evidence: Access reviews, control sampling, KPI reporting, and internal audit; nonconformities tracked in NH-NC-001.

Justification: Operational consistency requires documented procedures for critical activities.
Implementation evidence: Procedure set for onboarding, access review, incidents, backup, continuity, awareness, suppliers, and data subject requests.

Justification: Staff and contractors have access to sensitive health data and production systems.
Implementation evidence: Reference and CV checks are performed; criminal record and identity verification are not yet applied to all roles, and contractor screening is limited.

Justification: Employment and contractor terms must state security and confidentiality responsibilities.
Implementation evidence: Employment contracts include confidentiality and policy compliance; revised contractor agreement includes security schedule.

Annex A control: Information security awareness, education and training
Justification: Phishing and unsafe handling remain the most likely causes of compromise.
Implementation evidence: Quarterly awareness programme; 100 percent completion in Q1 2027; monthly phishing simulations with 3.4 percent failure rate in March 2027.

Justification: Deliberate or repeated policy breaches require a consistent response.
Implementation evidence: Employee handbook disciplinary process; contractor breach escalation in the supplier agreement.

Annex A control: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
Justification: Leavers and movers may retain access or knowledge that creates risk.
Implementation evidence: Offboarding checklist, exit interview, asset return, and access removal confirmation; sampled for 6 leavers.

Justification: Staff, contractors, and suppliers handle confidential patient and business data.
Implementation evidence: NDAs in employment contracts, revised Pixelwave agreement, and supplier contract template.

Justification: About 40 percent of staff work remotely on a typical day.
Implementation evidence: Remote working and mobile device policy; endpoint requirements; VPN and MFA for production access.

Justification: Staff and contractors must be able to report incidents and weaknesses promptly.
Implementation evidence: Reporting button in email, Slack channel, and incident mailbox; awareness training covers reporting; no-blame reporting statement.

Justification: The Cairo office contains endpoints, network equipment, and staff who access patient data.
Implementation evidence: Office access controlled by fob; reception and landlord lobby; perimeter checks recorded.

Justification: Unauthorized entry could lead to theft or network access.
Implementation evidence: Fob access, visitor sign-in and escort, and fob reconciliation against the staff list.

Justification: The network cupboard and support areas contain sensitive equipment.
Implementation evidence: Network cupboard locked and access logged; support floor separation; keys held by the Office Manager.

Justification: Reception and entry points require monitoring.
Implementation evidence: CCTV covers reception only; the network cupboard and support floor are not covered. A coverage review is scheduled for Q3 2027.

Annex A control: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
Justification: Fire, power loss, and building incidents could affect availability.
Implementation evidence: Building fire alarm and extinguishers; UPS for the network cupboard; landlord maintenance; incident escalation route.

Justification: Nabd has no designated secure areas. All office areas are open-plan and covered by the general physical controls in A.7.1 to A.7.4. The network cupboard is treated as a controlled area under A.7.3.
Implementation evidence: No secure areas exist; the network cupboard is locked and access logged under A.7.3.

Justification: Patient documents and screens are visible in an open-plan office.
Implementation evidence: Clear desk and clear screen rules; automatic screen lock; two quarterly spot checks completed.

Justification: Endpoints and network equipment require physical protection.
Implementation evidence: Equipment sited away from public areas; network cupboard locked; spare laptops stored in a locked cabinet.

Justification: Laptops, phones, and contractor devices leave the office daily.
Implementation evidence: Remote working policy, MDM, encryption, and incident reporting for lost or stolen devices.

Justification: Removable media could carry patient data or introduce malware.
Implementation evidence: Removable media restricted and encrypted; use requires approval; media handling rules in the information handling policy.

Justification: Power and connectivity support in-scope services.
Implementation evidence: UPS for network equipment; ISP redundancy through a secondary connection; building utilities maintained by the landlord.

Justification: Nabd does not manage structured cabling or server-room infrastructure. Cabling in the leased office is the landlord's responsibility and is covered by the lease; the network cupboard is controlled under A.7.3.
Implementation evidence: No Nabd-managed cabling infrastructure; lease defines landlord responsibility.

Justification: Device faults and maintenance can affect security and availability.
Implementation evidence: Manufacturer support and patching; maintenance performed by approved providers; device replacement process.

Annex A control: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
Justification: Devices leaving Nabd contain patient and employee data.
Implementation evidence: Certified wipe before disposal or reuse; disposal register; 9 wipe certificates in Q1 2027.

Justification: Endpoints are the primary access path to patient data and email.
Implementation evidence: Asset inventory, MDM enrolment, encryption enforcement, screen lock, and endpoint protection baselines.

Justification: Administrators can access all patient data and production configuration.
Implementation evidence: IAM Identity Center, per-person SSH certificates, admin role separation, session limits, and quarterly privileged access review.

Justification: Tenant isolation and least privilege are essential for a multi-tenant health platform.
Implementation evidence: Application tenant isolation by clinic ID; role-based access; least-privilege support roles; access reviews.

Justification: Source code and infrastructure code reveal security weaknesses and secrets.
Implementation evidence: GitHub organization 2FA, branch protection, least-privilege teams, and removal of former contractor access.

Justification: Weak or absent MFA enables account takeover and patient data exposure.
Implementation evidence: MFA enforced for Google, AWS, GitHub, and Admin Panel; phishing-resistant methods for administrators; OTP rate limits and device binding for patients.

Justification: Capacity shortfalls threaten the contracted 99.9 percent availability.
Implementation evidence: CloudWatch capacity metrics, autoscaling, monthly capacity review, and load testing before peak periods.

Justification: Phishing and endpoint compromise are credible threats.
Implementation evidence: Windows Defender and macOS protection enabled; EDR rollout planned for Q3 2027. No endpoint EDR at audit date.

Justification: Unpatched software and dependencies could be exploited.
Implementation evidence: Dependency, container, and infrastructure scanning; severity-based patch SLAs; annual penetration test completed.

Justification: Misconfiguration is a leading cause of cloud data exposure.
Implementation evidence: Terraform-managed infrastructure; security baselines for AWS, endpoints, and SaaS; configuration drift review.

Justification: PDPL storage limitation requires deletion when data is no longer needed.
Implementation evidence: Retention schedule; automated deletion jobs; legal hold process; deletion evidence retained.

Justification: Production data is used in staging and must not be exposed in identifiable form.
Implementation evidence: Masking pipeline covers 11 of 14 tables; 3 tables outstanding at internal audit (NC-01). Synthetic-data default for new tests.

Justification: Patient data can leak through email, chat, support tickets, and exports.
Implementation evidence: DLP rules for email and Slack, support data-handling rules, and export logging; no endpoint DLP.

Justification: Patient records and platform configuration must survive loss or corruption.
Implementation evidence: Daily RDS snapshots, S3 versioning, cross-region copies, 12-month monthly snapshots, and quarterly restore tests.

Justification: Availability commitments require resilient processing.
Implementation evidence: Multi-AZ application and RDS; single AWS region with cross-region backups and a documented DR plan.

Justification: Audit trails are required for patient record access, production changes, and investigations.
Implementation evidence: CloudTrail, CloudWatch, WAF, Google Workspace, and Admin Panel view and export logs; 12-month security log retention.

Justification: Alerts must be reviewed and acted on, not only generated.
Implementation evidence: GuardDuty, CloudTrail, WAF, and application alerts routed to on-call; weekly review record; triage runbook.

Justification: Correlated logs and evidence depend on accurate time.
Implementation evidence: AWS time synchronization for all cloud resources; endpoint time configured by MDM; NTP monitoring.

Justification: Administrative tools can bypass application and operating system controls.
Implementation evidence: No utility programs with control-override capability are installed; administrative tools restricted to managed hosts and named administrators.

Annex A control: Installation of software on operational systems
Justification: Unapproved software can introduce malware or licence risk.
Implementation evidence: Endpoint application allow-lists and admin restrictions; server images immutable and managed through CI/CD.

Justification: The platform and Admin Panel are exposed to the internet.
Implementation evidence: AWS WAF, security groups, private subnets, restricted Admin Panel ingress, and network configuration standards.

Justification: Network services must be configured and secured.
Implementation evidence: TLS 1.2 or higher, managed certificates, service configuration standards, and supplier assurance for cloud network services.

Justification: Production, non-production, office, and guest traffic require separation.
Implementation evidence: VPC public, private, and isolated subnets; separate production and non-production accounts; separate staff and guest Wi-Fi.

Justification: Malicious websites and phishing kits are a credible threat.
Implementation evidence: DNS filtering on the office network and browser protections on managed endpoints; no endpoint web proxy.

Justification: Patient data must be protected in transit and at rest.
Implementation evidence: TLS 1.2 or higher, AWS KMS encryption, encrypted backups, Secrets Manager, and a cryptography policy.

Justification: Nabd continuously develops and deploys its platform.
Implementation evidence: Secure development policy, security requirements, code review, SAST, dependency scanning, and release gates.

Justification: Security requirements must be defined before development.
Implementation evidence: Security requirements in the product backlog and definition of done; threat modelling for high-risk changes; DPIA trigger.

Annex A control: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
Justification: Architecture decisions determine the exposure of patient data.
Implementation evidence: Architecture principles and review; tenant isolation; least privilege; encryption by default; documented in the architecture diagram.

Justification: Coding errors can expose patient data or enable injection and authorization bypass.
Implementation evidence: Secure coding standards, peer review, SAST, dependency scanning, and secure coding training for engineers.

Annex A control: Security testing in development and acceptance
Justification: Security defects must be found before production.
Implementation evidence: SAST in CI, dependency and container scanning, DAST on staging, and an annual external penetration test.

Justification: Pixelwave developers contribute to mobile repositories and staging access.
Implementation evidence: Revised agreement, security schedule, access restrictions, code review, and contractor acknowledgement; contractor device assurance is limited.

Annex A control: Separation of development, test and production environments
Justification: Production data and code must be isolated from development activity.
Implementation evidence: Production and non-production AWS accounts are separate; development and staging share one account; masking is incomplete (NC-01).

Justification: Uncontrolled changes caused a three-hour outage in August 2026.
Implementation evidence: Change policy, pull-request approval, automated tests, emergency change approval, rollback testing, and post-implementation review.

Justification: Testing with production data requires protection.
Implementation evidence: Masking and synthetic data are the standard; three tables remain unmasked (NC-01); access to staging restricted.

Annex A control: Protection of information systems during audit testing
Justification: Internal and external audits require access to systems and evidence.
Implementation evidence: Audit access is read-only, time-bound, approved by the CTO, and logged; audit scope agreed in advance.
